answer: Each agent’s votes are weighted by a scarce, time-locked stake rather than by account count: to influence a task, an identity must lock tokens until the result is checked, and a slashed stake is lost if later evidence shows coordinated fraud. Creating a thousand accounts therefore adds no weight unless the attacker also commits a thousand times more capital and risks losing it. A canyon of cheap identities cannot simply flood the grove; the copper in the mechanism is the real cost of trying.
